messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the autotuner change on main (commit 4f8a) I'm seeing a latency regression for short sequences. p50 for seq=16 went from ~18ms -> ~28ms on a8g. p95 also bumped a bit. Long sequences (seq>=512) actually improved.

sara: Ugh. Do you have a profile dump? nvtx/nsys traces would help. :thinking_face:

alex: Pasted a small nsight summary for a short-job canary (batch=8, seq=16):
```
Kernel: transformer_forward_tile128   time: 22.3ms  regs: 56  local_mem: 7.1MB  occupancy: 30%
Kernel: kv_cache_read                   time: 0.8ms   regs: 18  local_mem: 0.2MB  occupancy: 70%
Kernel: softmax_tile32                  time: 1.6ms   regs: 42  local_mem: 1.1MB  occupancy: 40%
Spills: transformer_forward_tile128 -> 1.8MB local memory per block
```
Notice the main transformer kernel was chosen as tile128 path (higher throughput path) even though seq is small.

praveen: Looks like the kernel-picker opted for the high-occupancy / large-tile variant that wins on avg token throughput but has high register pressure (regs=56) and thus spills for short seq micro-batches. That explains higher latency due to local mem load/store.

jules: Did the autotuner recently change its cost model? We added throughput-weighted objective last sprint which may bias towards long-seq wins.

alex: Exactly. The new objective minimized tokens/sec across sampled workloads, which biases toward long-seq behavior. We didn't include a separate path for latency-sensitive short sequences.

sara: Quick mitigation idea: make kernel-picker aware of sequence-length buckets and topology. If seq < X -> prefer low-reg-path (tile32, warp-specialized) even if tokens/sec is lower for long runs. We should gather the per-model seq histogram and apply per-route thresholds.

praveen: Agreed. Also consider adding a microkernel variant with warp-specialization for short paths (split warps, reduce shared mem) — we did similar for matmul-actor. That reduces register pressure.

jules: Proposal pseudo-code:
```
if seq <= 64 and batch*seq < short_threshold:
  choose_kernel(policy='latency_short', prefer_low_regs=True)
else if seq >= 256:
  choose_kernel(policy='throughput_long')
else:
  choose_kernel(policy='balanced')
```
Also feed runtime seq histogram into tuner to adjust thresholds per model.

alex: I ran a quick local patch that forces tile32 kernel for seq=16: p50 -> 16.5ms, p95 -> 24ms. No regressions on long seq when run through canary. Will open PR with toggle and a small switch in the picker.

perf-bot: Canary results (canary-2027-03-15) attached: short-path enabled: p50 -26% for seq<=32, p95 -18%. Long seq unchanged within noise.

sara: Nice. What about KV cache behavior? Short-path reduces the transformer's register usage but does it increase KV read overhead due to smaller tile loops?

praveen: KV read stayed the same on profiler. The main cost was local-memory stalls from spills in the large-tile path. Once we avoid spills, KV overhead is negligible relatively.

jules: For rollout: canary -> 5% traffic on dedicated clusters with seq histogram gating, monitor p50/p95 and local_mem usage per kernel. If any model shows increased local_mem > 1MB per block, auto-fallback to previous picker.

alex: I'll add metrics: kernel_choice, regs, local_mem_per_block, seq_bucket to the console dashboard. Also logging the autotuner reason code so we can reproduce.

sara: Great. Follow-ups: (1) PR to add seq-bucketing to picker, (2) add warp-specialized microkernel for short path, (3) add canary gating and dashboard metrics. Assigning: alex (1+3), praveen (2), jules (review).

alex: Will open PR in a few hours. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

jules: If anyone runs more nsight traces, drop them here. Let's track regressions vs token-weighted objective and try adding a latency objective variant for latency-sensitive tenants.

perf-bot: Note: regression ticket created RW-3142 for tracking autotuner objective side effects.
